labels.notes: Row partial, unmarked; the file claims step (2) only, and its SCOPE says the tagged sorry of regM_isCauchyComplete_of_complete stays (step (3)). (1) Conclusion: LFSurgeryData.isCauchySurface_sigmaStar concludes (Causal.Flat.flatCausality 2 (e0RegMFlat M)).IsCauchySurface Dat.sigmaStarReg. That is the same predicate on the same kind of set (regSet M of Σ* = (S \ ⋃ spears) ∪ ⋃ cusps) as the strict E0Surgery.SurgeryData.isCauchySurface_sigmaStar (GX/BTZ/Surgery.lean:7425–7432), and sigmaStar_toSurgeryData is rfl, so the conclusion is not weaker. (2) Hypotheses: (CE M).GloballyHyperbolic, (CE M).IsCauchySurface S and an LFSurgeryData M S. The LFSurgeryData fields (SpearFamily.lean:152–161: countable ι, D, pt : ι ≃ S ∩ S0, pt_ray, disjoint, isClosed, locallyFinite, rimC1) and the SpearSurgeryDatum fields (Surgery.lean:2805–2833) are local chart and cusp data only: no finiteness, no Cauchy or acausality property of Σ*, no IsSpearArc hypothesis. Nothing the target has to prove is assumed. Local finiteness is an added structure field beyond the paper's « disjoint » (l.1574), but it is disclosed in the findings, and exists_lfSurgeryData_of_rimC1 (step (1), already audited) proves it exists under the paper's hypotheses, plus RimC1, which the _of_complete form discharges. The strict theorem's hrem (rem:curve_spear) is really discharged here by SpearSurgeryDatum.isSpearArc_of_inextensible (Surgery.lean:4160), whose hypotheses are GH and inextensibility only. E0-only, and Σ Cauchy weakened from smooth spacelike complete: both are disclosed in the checklist. (4) The l.1574–1575 finding is faithful and correctly hedged: the paper says only « disjoint spear neighborhoods » and gives no argument for infinitely many spears. The REPORT says local finiteness is sufficient and explicitly does not claim it is necessary (« not a counterexample »), so nothing false would go to the author. The finding that cor:intersect is not invoked directly (monotone height, Lemma 2.7, together with rem:curve_spear) is accurate.
